title: Meiosis and sexual reproduction
summary: How is the chromosome number halved, and where does variety come from?
cards.0.p: If gametes carried as many chromosomes as body cells, the chromosome number would double in every generation. Meiosis halves the chromosome number (2n → n). In animals it makes gametes, and in plants it makes spores.
cards.0.key: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, and fertilization doubles it. This keeps the number constant from one generation to the next.
cards.1.p: In a diploid cell, every chromosome has a partner. One comes from the mother and the other from the father. These partners are called homologous chromosomes. Homologs have the same length, shape and order of genes. Humans have 23 homologous pairs.
cards.1.key: Homologs can carry different alleles of the same gene. The X and Y in males are the exception. Homologs are the mother's and father's copies, while sister chromatids are copies of the same chromosome.
cards.1.once.soru: Of the 46 chromosomes in a human body cell, how many come from the mother?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: One of each pair comes from the mother and the other from the father.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: Not all 46 chromosomes come from a single parent.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: Half of them come from the mother.
cards.2.p: Before meiosis, DNA is copied once. In prophase I, homologous chromosomes line up side by side along their whole length. This is called synapsis. The structure of four chromatids is called a tetrad. Tetrads do not form in mitosis.
cards.2.key: A tetrad is one homologous pair. That means it is made of 2 chromosomes and 4 chromatids.
cards.3.p: In a tetrad, non-sister chromatids of the homologs cross over each other. This point is called a chiasma. The chromatids swap pieces here, and this is called crossing over. This creates chromatids that carry the mother's and father's genes together.
cards.3.key: Crossing over happens in prophase I, between non-sister chromatids.
cards.4.p: In metaphase I, the tetrads line up at the equator in pairs. In anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles, and the centromeres do not split. At the end of telophase I, two n cells form, but the chromosomes still have two chromatids.
cards.4.key: At the end of meiosis II, the chromosome number is also n. It becomes 2n only for a short time in anaphase II.
cards.5.p: DNA is not copied between meiosis I and meiosis II. Meiosis II is like mitosis, and in anaphase II the sister chromatids separate. The result is four haploid cells that are genetically different from one another.
cards.5.key: Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis I, and sister chromatids separate in meiosis II.
cards.5.once.soru: When a germ cell completes meiosis, how many cells form?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: Two divisions come one after the other. One cell first becomes two, then four.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: In meiosis, the cell divides twice. That is why four cells form, not two.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: DNA is copied once, but the cell divides twice. The result is 4 cells.
cards.6.h: DNA and chromosome number in meiosis
cards.6.p: In a cell with 2n = 4, the amount of DNA rises from 2 units to 4 units in the S phase. It drops to 2 units in telophase I and to 1 unit in telophase II. The number of chromosomes drops from 4 to 2 in meiosis I.
cards.6.key: When the centromeres split in anaphase II, the chromosome number becomes 4 for a short time, then drops back to 2 at the end. Meiosis II halves the amount of DNA, not the chromosome number.
cards.6.once.soru: In which division of meiosis is the chromosome number halved?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: When the homologs separate, each cell gets only one of each pair. This drops the number from 2n to n.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: Meiosis II separates sister chromatids. By this stage, the chromosome number is already n.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: The chromosome number is halved only once, in meiosis I.
cards.7.p: Both mitosis and meiosis start with DNA copying. Mitosis allows growth, repair and asexual reproduction, and it keeps the chromosome number the same. Meiosis makes gametes or spores, halves the chromosome number and creates variety.
cards.7.key: A haploid (n) cell can go through mitosis, but not meiosis.
cards.8.p: There are three sources of variety. The first is crossing over. The second is the independent assortment of homologs in metaphase I. This creates 2n kinds of gametes, and in humans that number is about 8.4 million. The third is the random joining of gametes at fertilization.
cards.8.key: The n in the 2ⁿ formula is the number of homologous pairs. One mother and father can produce about 70 trillion different zygotes, and crossing over raises this number even further.
cards.9.p: The nondisjunction you just saw leads to gametes with n+1 and n−1 chromosomes. In Down syndrome, there are three copies of chromosome 21, and the total chromosome number is 47. This risk rises as the mother gets older.
cards.9.key: If nondisjunction happens in meiosis I, all 4 gametes are abnormal. If it happens in meiosis II, usually 2 gametes are abnormal.
cards.10.p: In males, one germ cell gives four equal cells, which means four sperm. This is called spermatogenesis. In females, the cytoplasm does not divide equally. One large egg and small polar bodies form. This is called oogenesis.
cards.10.key: The polar bodies break down, and the nutrients gather in the egg. One germ cell gives 4 sperm in males and 1 egg in females.
cards.10.once.soru: How many eggs does one egg mother cell give through meiosis?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: The cytoplasm does not divide equally. One cell becomes the egg, and the others become small polar bodies.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: In males four sperm form, but in females only one egg forms.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: The polar bodies do not become eggs. Only one egg forms.
cards.11.p: The joining of the sperm and egg nuclei is called fertilization. Two n gametes join and form a 2n zygote. In fish and frogs, external fertilization happens in water. In reptiles, birds and mammals, internal fertilization happens inside the female's body.
cards.11.key: The zygote divides by mitosis and forms the embryo. In external fertilization, many gametes are released. Internal fertilization is an adaptation to life on land.
cards.11.etk.soru: Sort each animal by how fertilization happens.
cards.11.etk.ogeler.1.2: A frog releases its eggs and sperm into water. Fertilization happens outside the body.
cards.11.etk.ogeler.4.2: A dolphin lives in water, but it is a mammal. Fertilization happens inside the female's body.
cards.11.once.soru: How many sets of chromosomes does the zygote formed by fertilization carry?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: A sperm (n) and an egg (n) join. So n + n = 2n.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: Gametes are the ones with n chromosomes. A zygote forms when two gametes join.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: Each gamete brings one set of chromosomes. That makes two sets in total.
cards.12.p: In asexual reproduction, a single parent gives offspring like itself. This is fast, but there is little variety. Sexual reproduction involves meiosis and fertilization. The offspring differ both from their parents and from one another.
cards.12.key: In asexual reproduction, variety arises only through mutation.
cards.12.once.soru: If conditions suddenly change, which population has a better chance of survival?
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: The offspring differ from one another. That is why some of them can adapt to the new conditions.
cards.12.once.secenekler.1.neden: The individuals are nearly all the same, so one change affects them all at once.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: Variety is a big advantage in a changing environment.
cards.13.p:
• In meiosis, DNA is copied once, the cell divides twice and 4 different n cells form.
• Homologs separate in meiosis I, and sister chromatids separate in meiosis II.
• Variety comes from crossing over, independent assortment and random fertilization.
• Nondisjunction leads to outcomes such as Down syndrome.
• In plants, spores form by meiosis and gametes by mitosis.
quiz.0.q: Put the events of meiosis in order.
quiz.0.ogeler.1: Homologs pair up into tetrads and cross over
quiz.0.ogeler.2: Tetrads line up in pairs at the equator
quiz.0.ogeler.3: Homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles
quiz.0.ogeler.4: Sister chromatids move to opposite poles
quiz.0.e: DNA is copied once before meiosis. In prophase I, tetrads form and crossing over happens. In metaphase I the tetrads line up in pairs, and in anaphase I the homologs separate. In anaphase II the sister chromatids separate, and four n cells form.
quiz.1.q: In an organism with 2n = 8, the homologs differ from each other and there is no crossing over. How many kinds of gametes can form by independent assortment?
quiz.1.e: The number of homologous pairs is n = 4. Independent assortment gives 2<sup>4</sup> = 16 kinds of gametes.
quiz.2.q: Sort each event by the division it happens in.
quiz.2.ogeler.3.0: Can happen in a haploid cell
quiz.2.e: Tetrads, crossing over and homologs separating are unique to meiosis. A haploid cell can only go through mitosis, and mitosis gives identical cells. DNA copying, centromeres splitting and spindle fibers are found in both divisions.
quiz.3.q: In a human (2n = 46), meiosis I goes normally. In meiosis II, the sister chromatids of one chromosome fail to separate in just one of the two cells. What are the chromosome numbers of the four gametes?
quiz.3.e: At the end of meiosis I, both cells have 23 chromosomes. The cell with nondisjunction gives gametes with 24 and 22 chromosomes, and the normal cell gives gametes with 23 and 23.
quiz.3.y.0: This pattern belongs to nondisjunction in meiosis I. In meiosis II, only one cell is affected.
quiz.3.y.2: The two gametes from the cell with nondisjunction cannot be normal. One gets an extra chromosome, and the other is missing one.
quiz.3.y.3: Gametes are haploid. 47 and 45 chromosomes can only appear after fertilization, in the zygote.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Build a tetrad, swap pieces, play through meiosis and count the gametes.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Look at the generations, then turn on meiosis in the gametes.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: In humans, gametes have 23 chromosomes, and the zygote has 23 + 23 = 46. This keeps the number the same from one generation to the next.
A:adimlar.1.metin: The DNA was copied before meiosis. Now bring the homologous chromosomes side by side in prophase I.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: How many chromatids are in a tetrad?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: 2 is the number of chromosomes. Each chromosome has been copied, so it has two chromatids.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: 8 is the total number of chromatids in this cell. A tetrad is just one homologous pair.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A tetrad is made of two homologous chromosomes. Each has 2 chromatids, so a tetrad has 4 chromatids.
A:adimlar.2.metin: These chromatids carry the genes A and B. Swap the pieces and look at the gene combinations.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.tamam: At first there were only the combinations AB and ab. After the swap, Ab and aB formed too. These are new chromatids that carry the mother's and father's genes together.
A:adimlar.3.metin: In meiosis, DNA is copied once, but the cell divides twice. In this cell 2n = 4. Make a guess before you play.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: What moves to opposite poles in anaphase I?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Sister chromatids separate in meiosis II, in anaphase II.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate and the centromeres do not split. This is where the chromosome number is halved (n).
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Chromatids do not come apart in meiosis I. Chromosomes with two chromatids go to each pole.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Change the number of homologous pairs and build a cell that makes 8 kinds of gametes.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: With 3 homologous pairs, 2³ = 8 kinds of gametes form. With the 23 human pairs, this number is over 8 million.
A:adimlar.5.metin: Sometimes homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids fail to separate. This is called nondisjunction. In this human cell, one homologous pair does not separate in meiosis I, while meiosis II goes normally. Make a guess first, then play.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: Of the 4 gametes that form, how many have an abnormal chromosome number?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The pair that did not separate goes to one cell as an extra, and the other cell gets none.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: For two gametes to be abnormal, the nondisjunction has to happen in meiosis II and in only one cell.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The pair that did not separate goes to a single cell, and both cells are affected. That is why all four gametes are abnormal: 24, 24, 22 and 22.
A:adimlar.6.metin: Switch between mitosis and meiosis and compare the cells that form.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.soru: Which one is seen only in meiosis?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Both divisions start with DNA copying in interphase.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Homologs pair up only in prophase I. Tetrads and crossing over are not seen in mitosis.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Sister chromatids separate both in the anaphase of mitosis and in anaphase II of meiosis.
A:kapanis.0: Meiosis halves the chromosome number (2n → n), and fertilization doubles it. This keeps the number constant from one generation to the next.
A:kapanis.1: In meiosis, DNA is copied once and the cell divides twice. Homologs separate in meiosis I, sister chromatids separate in meiosis II and 4 haploid cells form at the end.
A:kapanis.2: In prophase I, homologs form a tetrad. Non-sister chromatids swap pieces by crossing over.
A:kapanis.3: The sources of variety are crossing over, independent assortment (2ⁿ gametes) and random fertilization.
A:kapanis.4: Nondisjunction makes gametes with n+1 and n−1 chromosomes. Down syndrome (47 chromosomes) is one example.
